glosses: to push through (to force (legislation) to be passed)
To overcome (pain, discomfort, etc.) by force or willpower.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see push, through.

examples.text: The corridor was so packed with people that I had to push through.

glosses: To subject to an excessive demand on strength, resources, abilities, or the imagination.

examples.text: The very phrase of "generous forbearance" shocked her as overstrained; but she did marvel that Lord Avonleigh felt neither pained nor embarrassed in a situation where such sensations seemed inevitable.
Clover warned him sometimes to be careful not to overstrain himself, but Boxer would never listen to her.

glosses: A person's self: general form of himself, herself, themself or yourself.

examples.text: Teaching oneself to swim can be dangerous.
If attending to your childhood wounds and responding with kindness feels selfish, it is important to remember that compassion for oneself often makes people more compassionate to others, Lev said.
